utterances.text: As far as I remember, a year and a half, up to two years perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: Then, at one point in time, we simply learned, or rather we were told that the weapons had to go to Banja Luka, that they were again being relocated from the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you be now a little bit more specific about the time when you learned that the weapons should go to Banja Luka? Which period of time we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was towards the end of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And were these weapons really transferred to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Were you able to check whether these weapons are in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: Yes, on one occasion.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And where in Banja Luka were they taken?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: The weapons were stored in a JNA barracks in Banja Luka but I cannot remember the name of the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We already mentioned that there were elections in 1990, and it was one of the reasons why these weapons were moved from the TO warehouse. Do you know the results of the elections in Donji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: I know that SDA and SDS won the elections, but that other parties also participated in the government with a smaller number of candidates who became deputies at the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness Exhibit P1700. It is a document from January 30th of January, 1991, issued by Serbian Democratic Party of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Donji Vakuf, and it says, among others, "Proportional representation of the peoples and nationalities of Bosnia and Herzegovina must be ensured in the assembly of the social, political communities" and there are these two versions of distribution of power. If you have a look at these two versions, can you make a comment whether the -- at first the distribution was proportional or not?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: It was, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And you had the opportunity yesterday to have a look at this document. Which of these variants -- versions, I'm sorry, which of these two versions was the one which was at the end accepted?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: I believe that ultimately, the final decision came closer to variant 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Now I will show you Exhibit P1701. It is a list of persons selected and appointed by the Donji Vakuf municipal assembly. To your knowledge, was -- were these people appointed to the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: These are not the people who were appointed to the municipal assembly. These people were appointed by the municipal assembly to certain offices.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And does the offices correspond with the power distribution as agreed?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: They do, roughly, with the proviso that certain people do not occupy the posts which they actually had, to which they were later elected. What we see here is a draft.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Under .7 is Senad Alkic. Were you approved for the position?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And can you see any names which weren't approved or didn't hold the position as stated in this document?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: I'll try, as far as I can remember. Mirko Zagorac did not eventually become president of the executive board. Mile Ilic was the secretary of the municipal Secretariat for National Defence. The rest of the appointments correspond to this proposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm done with this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You already confirmed that in 1989, you were -- you became the commander of the TO. Is it correct that from that date, you started drafting your diary?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: I had kept my diary in a notebook even earlier, and I just continued throughout the period when I was the commander to write everything that was of interest and related to my new duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And do you remember approximately when you started and when you finished with your entries in this diary?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: I've always kept a diary. This particular notebook which I made available to you was finished when I stopped going to my job, that is the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of this diary?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: It was a working notebook of sorts. I used it as a reminder of what I was supposed to do, how to carry out my regular tasks and duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you -- did you also record issues which were discussed at any meetings?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have this diary here. There are many pages of this diary. However, the Prosecution intends to tender into evidence only part of this diary, and it is part which was translated and the Defence has the full version of the diary in his possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you agree with that, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I have the B/C/S version, full, and I have part of it translated, just like she said, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. It's not that I was questioning it's just I wanted a confirmation from the Defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So I intend to tender into evidence the part of the diary which starts with ERN number 0207-2292 until 0207-2307, for which translation is provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, that bears absolutely no relationship to what I have. The one I have is 0306-0158 through 0306-0167.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It is the translation of the document I just stated, what I said was ERN number of the original document and so just for the record I can state that the translation of the original document is 0306 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does that make sense to you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay we can proceed now, Ms. Richterova.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to tender into evidence this part of the diary under the number P1693.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Before I -- you can leave the diary with the witness. And until I go through the diary thoroughly, I just want the witness to make comment on the entry which is on the second page, which is marked 0207-2293, in the original language, and in the translation, it is really the second page, 0306-0159. And it says, among others, "Possibility of reviewing weapons, possibility of returning some of the weapons." And headline was, "Agreement with executive committee and municipal assembly presidents." Can you tell us what were you referring to in these two entries?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: This was an agreement reached between the President of the executive committee, who was a Serb by ethnicity, and the president of the municipal assembly, who was a Muslim. Bearing in mind that the weapons were already in Banja Luka by that time, we were trying to reach an agreement and to go there to inspect our weaponry, to also review the possibility of getting a part of this weaponry back in order to be able to place a certain number of Territorial Defence units into operation if required.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And did you get any weapons back?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Now I would change the subject for a while and go back to Territorial Defence. Where this Territorial Defence sit? Where did you sit?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: I personally sat in the building of the municipal assembly of Donji Vakuf on the third floor, in an annex to the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And Territorial Defence, did you have any responsibilities towards the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you just briefly describe?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: Since we were on the payroll of the municipal assembly, we had the obligation of reporting to the municipal assembly about the implementation of our tasks and duties concerning the resources that had been invested in the purchase of weapons, military equipment, ammunition, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And you just said that, "We had the obligation of reporting to the municipal assembly." Did you attend meetings of municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: Rarely but I did sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And did you attend meetings in 1990 -- towards the end of 1991, beginning 1992?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: I believe I attended those meetings and I knew their agenda and the deliberations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And can you just briefly tell us what was the relationship between Territorial Defence and the JNA?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: Municipal TO staffs, Territorial Defence staffs, were technically reporting to the district TO staffs, whereas district TO staffs were subordinated to the republican TO staff. In that sense, municipal staffs had nothing to do with JNA units, apart from possible coordination, which happened only at somebody's own initiative, if it happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And were members of JNA also members of the TO, either on the republic or district level?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: In the municipal TO staff, there were no active-duty military personnel who used to serve in the JNA. In the district staff, there were some, starting with the commander, his deputy, and some other officers. There were people who used to be former JNA members and who served in the republican TO staff. That goes for the district staff as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And do you know what was their role within the TO?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: Their role was similar to the one they had in municipal staffs. They did the job as prescribed by the law for the units and staffs of the municipal Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And can you be more -- can you elaborate on this, when you are stating that they did the job as prescribed by the law?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: That meant that the republican staff, district staff, and the municipal staff, as the lowest instance, were responsible for the training of reserve units of the Territorial Defence, also for carrying out mobilisation and for the logistical support of those units in the course of mobilisation and afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And I will ask you before the adjournment just one last question. When we were talking about these weapons which were in premises of all kind of enterprises, all kind of companies, can you tell us what kind of weapons were in possession of these enterprises?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC
utterances.text: We had weapons of older models, old M-48 rifles, semi-automatic rifles, and the quantity of the weapons depended on the size of the enterprise, so to say, and of the financial status of the company concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I think we reached the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Richterova, I thank you. Sir, we have to stop now. We will continue tomorrow in the afternoon, when it's expected that you will finish with your testimony in this Tribunal. You will now be escorted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, do you have a clue as to whether you are receiving assistance tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'll have somebody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have a confirmation?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just wanted to confirm that with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yeah, no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So that's it. We will adjourn until tomorrow afternoon, 2.15. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 1.46 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 28th day of February, 2003, at 2.15 p.m.
